fact_en: Did you know gold never rusts? Even after many years, it keeps its beautiful shine!
fact_bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang bulawan dili magkalawang? Bisan paglabay sa daghang tuig, magpabilin pa rin kining masinaw!

findings.note: title_bis "Ang Bulawan Dili Makaunod" for "Gold Never Rusts". "Unod" is flesh/meat/contents; "dili makaunod" says nothing about rusting, so the title's claim is unreadable rather than true. The body has the correct word ("dili magkalawang"), and across ~250 rust cards the corpus consistently uses taya/kalawang - "makaunod" occurs only in this one card, marking the title as the defect.

fact_en:
What do limestone rocks and seashells have in common?

They are both made mostly of calcium carbonate! It is the exact same chemical that makes up seashells and snail shells.
fact_bis:
Unsay pagkapareho sa mga bato nga limestone ug mga kabibe?

Pareho silang halos puro calcium carbonate! Kini ang samang kemikal nga naghimo sa mga kabibe ug kabhang.

findings.note: title_bis "Limestone ug Bingkil" for "Limestone and Seashells". Cebuano "bingkil" means a quarrel/falling-out, not a shell; shell is kabibe or kabhang - which is exactly what this card's own body uses twice ("mga kabibe", "kabhang"). The title therefore names a different thing than the English. Same swap appears in ffct-10315 ("Shells Protect Clams" -> "Bingkil Tahong", body again uses kabhang), so it is a systematic wrong word, not a regional variant.

fact_en: The universe is super old — about 13.8 billion years! Scientists figured this out from solid scientific evidence.
fact_bis: Ang uniberso karaan kaayo — mga 13.8 ka bilyon ka tuig! Nahibaw-an kini sa mga siyentipiko gikan sa siyentipikong ebidensya.

findings.note: title_bis "Edad sa Kalibutan" for "Age of the Universe", with the body giving 13.8 billion years. "Kalibutan" is the world/Earth, and this same batch uses it that way twice (ffct-29705 "71% Tubig sa Kalibutan" = Earth's surface; ffct-29655 "presyur sulod sa Kalibutan" = inside the Earth). A child reading the title plus the number is set up to believe the Earth is 13.8 billion years old; the body's word "uniberso" is the correct one and is what the title should have used.

fact_en:
Can plates just slide past each other?

Yes! At some boundaries, plates slide past each other in opposite directions — and that grinding can cause earthquakes!
fact_bis:
Mahimo bang maglampasanay ang mga plaka?

Oo! Sa ubang utlanan, maglampasanay ang mga plaka sa magkasumpaki nga direksyon — ug ang pagkiskisan maoy makapahinabog linog!

findings.note: title_bis "Nagsapaw nga mga Plaka" = OVERLAPPING/stacked plates (sapaw = to overlay), which is the convergent/subduction picture, not the transform boundary the card is about. The body uses the correct verb "maglampasanay ... sa magkasumpaki nga direksyon". The heading alone teaches the wrong plate relationship.

fact_en:
Why does soil slide easily on clay?

Sometimes soil sits on a layer of clay. When the clay fills with water, it gets slippery like soap, making the soil on top slide downhill easily!
fact_bis:
Nganong sayon modahili ang yuta sa clay?

Usahay, ang yuta anaa sa ibabaw sa patong sa clay. Kung mapuno kini sa tubig, mahimo kining danlog sama sa sabon, mao nga sayon modahili paubos ang yuta!

findings.note: title_bis "Clay nga Lipad-lipad" — lipad/lupad is FLYING, not slippery; the card's key property (clay turns danlog, slippery, when waterlogged) is missing from the heading, which instead names flight. Body uses the correct word: "mahimo kining danlog sama sa sabon". Lower severity than the others (the heading is nonsense rather than false), but it is a title wrong-word with the correct word present in the same card.

fact_en: Nearby lightning makes a sharp crack, but far-off lightning makes a long rumble! This happens because sound reaches us from different parts of the bolt.
fact_bis: Ang duol nga kilat mohimo og hait nga putok, apan ang layo nga kilat taas nga lagubo! Mahitabo kini kay ang tingog moabot gikan sa lain-laing bahin sa kilat.

findings.note: title_bis "Butkon ug Kurug sa Kulog" — butkon is bukton, the ARM, not a thunder crack; kurug is a shiver/tremble, not a rumble. The heading reads "Arm and Shiver of Thunder". The body has both correct words ("hait nga putok" for the crack, "taas nga lagubo" for the rumble), so the title is the outlier and names a different thing entirely.

fact_en: Thunder is just a loud sound and cannot hurt you, but the lightning that makes it is dangerous!
fact_bis: Ang dalugdog tingog ra ug dili ka masakitan, apan ang kilat nga naghimo niini delikado!

findings.note: title_bis "Ang Kulog Tunod Ra" — tunod in Cebuano is to sink/set (as the sun does), so the heading loses the card's entire point ("Thunder Is Just Sound"). Almost certainly a slip for tunog; the body carries the correct Cebuano "Ang dalugdog tingog ra". Flagged because the whole claim lives in the title and the word that lands there means something else.

fact_en:
How does a rainbow form?

It forms when sunlight shines through raindrops in the air, separating into beautiful different colors!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa balangaw?

Maporma kini kung moagi ang silaw sa adlaw sa mga tulo sa ulan, mabahinbahin sa lainlaing bulok!

findings.note: title_bis "Pagbuto sa Bahaghari" = "The EXPLOSION of the Rainbow" (Cebuano buto = explode/burst; buto-as-seed is the Tagalog sense). The English is "How Rainbows Form", and the card's own body uses the correct word twice — "Unsaon pagporma sa balangaw? / Maporma kini...". The title names a different event than the card teaches.

fact_en:
What is an aurora?

An aurora is shimmering green or pink light in the sky near Earth's poles! It forms when tiny particles from the sun hit the air high in the atmosphere.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang aurora?

Ang aurora mao ang nagkidlap nga lunhaw o rosas nga kahayag sa langit duol sa mga poste sa Kalibutan! Maporma kini kung moigo ang gagmay nga tipik gikan sa adlaw sa hangin sa atmospera.

findings.note: "kahayag sa langit duol sa mga poste sa Kalibutan" — poste in Cebuano is a POST/PILLAR (lamppost), not a geographic pole (polo). Nothing else in this card restores it: no amihanan/habagatan, no polo. The card's single locating fact (auroras occur near Earth's poles) is unrecoverable; the child reads "near the Earth's posts". ffct-29876 in the same batch uses "polo" correctly, so poste is the outlier.

fact_en:
Can we see auroras in the Philippines?

Usually no, because we are near the equator! Auroras are seen most often in places close to Earth's north or south poles.
fact_bis:
Makita ba nato ang aurora sa Pilipinas?

Kasagaran dili, kay duol ta sa ekwador! Mas sagad makita ang aurora sa mga dapit nga duol sa amihanan o habagatang poste sa Kalibutan.

findings.note: title_bis "Aurora sa Ekwador" (Aurora at the Equator) states the OPPOSITE of the card: EN title is "Auroras Near the Poles" and the body says auroras are seen near the north/south poles and usually NOT here because we are near the equator. A child reading the heading alone learns that auroras happen at the equator. Same card's body also uses "poste sa Kalibutan" for the poles (poste = post/pillar); the corpus's own correct word is "polo" (ffct-29876: "sa mga polo").

fact_en:
Do rainbows only appear when it rains?

Nope! You can see them in waterfall, fountain, or garden hose spray when the sun shines. You just need light and tiny water droplets!
fact_bis:
Sa ulan lang ba mogawas ang balangaw?

Dili! Makita pod nimo kini sa tinilamsik sa busay, tubod, o hose kung silawan sa adlaw. Kinahanglan lang og kahayag ug gagmay nga tulo sa tubig!

findings.note: Tagalog false friend in title_bis "Rainbow sa Talon". Tagalog talon = waterfall; Cebuano talon = to jump/leap (waterfall is busay). The card's OWN body uses the correct word — "sa tinilamsik sa busay, tubod, o hose" — which is the strongest evidence the title is the outlier. Heading reads "Rainbow at the Jump".

fact_en:
How does a warmer climate affect crops in the Philippines?

Some areas may face longer and harsher droughts that can damage their crops!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pag-apekto sa mas init nga klima sa mga tanom sa Pilipinas?

Ang pipila ka lugar mahimong makasinati og mas taas ug mas grabe nga huwaw nga makadaot sa mga tanom!

findings.note: title_bis "Kahuol ug Pananom" — kahuol is anguish/breathlessness, not drought (huwaw/hulaw). The English title is "Droughts and Crops" and the body correctly uses "huwaw"; the title never names the drought.
